faq.q: What is the origin of Isaam?
faq.a: Isaam is associated with Arabic. Isaam is Arabic عِصَام (ʿIṣām) 'protector, safeguard, guardian', from the root ع ص م (ʿ-ṣ-m). CRITICAL SOURCE ERROR: the source gave عيسام (a different form) and glossed the name 'Given by God'; the correct form is عِصَام. Same name as isam and issam.
Yes — the underlying form عصام is Arabic.
Isaam can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.

faq.q: What does Isaam mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Isaam is rendered عصام and carries the sense عصام، نگهبان، پاسدار.
A romanized syllable approximation is i-saam. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Isaam?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Isaam, isaam, isam. Script forms are عصام, इसाम.

faq.q: Is Isaam a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
